transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what has been bothering you lately that brought you in to see me today?

Lately my mood has been all over the place, but a lot of the time I feel way too revved up and on edge. I get really irritable over tiny things and then swing into feeling almost overly “up,” like I have too much energy and can’t seem to calm down.
During these “revved up” or overly “up” times, do you also need much less sleep than usual and still feel full of energy, or are you mainly feeling tense and anxious but still tired or worn out?

When I’m in those really “up” phases, I sleep a lot less but still feel wired and full of energy. I might only get 3–4 hours of sleep and wake up feeling like I have to keep moving, not really tired even though I know I didn’t sleep much.

When you’re in those very “up” phases, have you ever had experiences like feeling invincible, believing you had special powers or a special mission, or seeing or hearing things that others don’t seem to notice?
I haven’t really felt invincible or like I have special powers or some kind of mission. And I don’t think I’ve seen or heard things that other people don’t—I haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you ever had periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt very down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, with low energy or loss of interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I’ve had stretches like that, and they’ve actually gone on much longer than just two weeks—more like months at a time. During those times I feel really down most of the day, barely have any energy, lose interest in pretty much everything, and tend to pull back from people and things I usually care about.

Have you ever had a period of at least a week where your mood was so high or irritable and your energy so increased that it clearly caused major problems in your life—like getting into serious trouble at work or school, damaging relationships, or needing to be hospitalized or evaluated in an emergency room?

Yeah, I’ve had a stretch like that recently that went on for about a month. I was so wound up and irritable that I snapped at coworkers and my boss, got written up at work, and had a couple of really bad blow‑ups with family to the point where they were worried I needed urgent help, though I didn’t actually go to the ER or get hospitalized.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were [F30.1, F31.0]. The patient reports recurrent, months‑long episodes of clearly depressive symptoms (low mood, low energy, anhedonia, social withdrawal) meeting the duration for a major depressive episode, along with at least one episode of markedly elevated/irritable mood and increased energy lasting about a month, with clear functional impairment (work write‑up, severe interpersonal conflicts, family concern about need for urgent help). There is no history of psychotic symptoms. This pattern indicates a bipolar course (both depressive and elevated episodes) rather than a single hypomanic episode without depression. Therefore a pure hypomanic episode diagnosis is no longer appropriate, and the current candidate is the bipolar spectrum code that includes hypomanic episodes with depressive episodes and no psychosis. Thus the list narrows from [F30.1, F31.0] to [F31.0].

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has clear episodes of abnormally elevated/irritable mood with markedly increased energy, decreased need for sleep, and significant functional impairment (work write‑ups, major interpersonal conflicts) lasting about a month, consistent with a manic episode. They also report recurrent, prolonged depressive episodes lasting months with low mood, anhedonia, low energy, and social withdrawal. There is no history of psychotic symptoms. This pattern supports bipolar affective disorder, current episode hypomanic or manic without psychotic symptoms; given the information provided and the candidate list, F31.0 (Bipolar affective disorder, current episode hypomanic) is selected as the closest match among the offered codes.
